chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام wrote to Muḥammad ibn Sinān, in what he wrote as an answer to his questions:

Allah has forbidden the killing of the soul because of the corruption of creation that would result from permitting it, their destruction, and the corruption of order. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has forbidden disobedience to parents because of what it contains of departing from reverence for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and reverence for the parents, ingratitude for the blessing, nullifying gratitude, and what that leads to of a decrease in offspring and its cessation, due to what is in undutifulness of diminished respect for the parents, recognizing their right, severing kinship ties, the parents becoming disinclined toward the child, and abandoning upbringing because of the child's abandonment of dutifulness toward them. And Allah, Exalted, has forbidden zina because of the corruption in it: killing souls, loss of lineages, neglect of children's upbringing, corruption of inheritances, and other similar aspects of corruption. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden accusing chaste women because of what it contains of corruption of lineages, denial of the child, nullifying inheritances, abandoning upbringing, loss of social knowledge and ties, and because of the grave sins and causes that lead to the corruption of creation.

And He has forbidden consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly for many reasons among the aspects of corruption. The first of that is that when a person consumes the wealth of the orphan unjustly, he has assisted in killing him, for the orphan is not self-sufficient, cannot manage for himself, has no one standing over his affairs, and has no one to care for him sufficiently like the care of his parents. So when one consumes his wealth, it is as though he has killed him and reduced him to poverty and need, along with what Allah has forbidden regarding it and what He has assigned for it of punishment in His saying, Mighty and Majestic:
And let those fear who, if they left behind weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them be wary of Allah and speak a right word.

And due to the saying of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: 'Indeed Allah has promised, regarding consuming the wealth of the orphan, two punishments: a punishment in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter.' Thus, in forbidding the orphan's wealth there is preservation of the orphan, his self-sufficiency, and safety for one's descendants from being afflicted by what afflicted him, because of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has promised therein of punishment, along with what is in that of the orphan seeking vengeance when he matures, and the occurrence of rancor, enmity, and hatred until they destroy one another. And Allah has forbidden fleeing from the battlefield because of the weakness in religion contained in it, making light of the messengers and the just Imams عليهم السلام, abandoning support for them against enemies, and incurring punishment for denying what they called to of acknowledgment of lordship, manifesting justice, abandoning oppression and its causing to die, and corruption. Also because of what that contains of emboldening the enemy against the Muslims, and what may occur in that of captivity, killing, nullifying the truth of the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and other corruption. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden reverting to Bedouin life after migration because of returning away from religion, abandoning assistance to the Prophets and the divine proofs عليهم السلام, and what is in that of corruption and nullifying the right of every rightful person—not because of merely dwelling in the desert. Therefore, if a man were to know the religion completely, it would not be permissible for him to dwell with the people of ignorance and fear for him, because one is not secure from his falling into abandoning knowledge, entering in with the people of ignorance, and persisting in that.

And the reason for the prohibition of riba is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden concerning it and what it contains of corruption of wealth, because when a person buys one dirham for two dirhams, the price of the dirham is one dirham and the price of the other is invalid. So the selling and buying of riba is loss in every state for the buyer and for the seller. Therefore Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited riba to the servants because of the corruption of wealth, just as He prohibited that the foolish person be handed his wealth because of what is feared regarding his corrupting it, until his sound judgment is perceived. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited riba, and the sale of riba is the sale of one dirham for two dirhams. And the reason for prohibiting riba after the proof has been made clear is what it contains of making light of the forbidden haram. It is a major sin after clarification and Allah's prohibition of it; such conduct is nothing but making light of the forbidden haram, and making light of that is entry into kufr. And the reason for prohibiting deferred riba is the disappearance of kindness, destruction of wealth, people's desire for profit, and their abandoning lending, while lending is among the means of kindness, and because of what is in that of corruption, ظلم, and the annihilation of wealth.

key_terms.التَّعَرُّبَ بَعْدَ الْهِجْرَةِ: reverting to Bedouin life after migration away from disbelief or ignorance
key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury or unlawful increase in financial exchange
key_terms.الزِّنَا: illicit sexual relations outside lawful marriage
key_terms.الْفِرَارَ مِنَ الزَّحْفِ: fleeing from battle in the face of the enemy
key_terms.عُقُوقَ الْوَالِدَيْنِ: undutifulness and disobedience toward one's parents
key_terms.قَذْفَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ: falsely accusing chaste women of sexual misconduct
key_terms.مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ: the property and wealth belonging to an orphan

ai.seo_question: What reasons does Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام give for the prohibition of major sins like zina, consuming an orphan’s wealth, and riba?
ai.summary: This hadith-letter from Imam ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā عليه السلام explains the wisdom behind several major prohibitions, including murder, undutifulness to parents, zina, false accusation, consuming an orphan's wealth, fleeing the battlefield, reverting after hijrah, and riba. It presents these rulings as protections for religion, family, lineage, social order, justice, and the sound circulation of wealth.
